chapter_title_en: Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.english_translation: When he saw, the heart of the knight leaped up and was lightened; here to him, distressed, joy became not tenfold, but a thousandfold; the rose (of his cheeks) brightened its colour, the crystal (of his face) became crystal (indeed), the jet (of his eyes) grew jetty; like a whirlwind he galloped down, he rested not from gazing at him.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 866; Wardrop Stanza 847): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა შეხედნა, ყმასა გულმან გაუფეთქნა, გაუნათდა,
აქა ლხინი დაღრეჯილსა უათასდა, არ უათდა;
ვარდმან ფერი განანათლა, ბროლი ბროლდა, სათი სათდა,
და ვით გრიგალმან ჩაირბინა, არ მოსცალდა ჭვრეტად მათდა.
stanzas.english_translation: When he saw Tariel he was indeed grieved; (Tariel) sat with drawn face in a state near unto death, his collar was rent, his head was all torn, he could no longer feel, he had stepped forth from the world.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 867; Wardrop Stanza 848): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა ტარიელ დაინახა, განაღამცა დაეღრიჯა:
ახლოს მყოფი სიკვდილისა ჯდა და პირი დაებღნიჯა,
საყელონი გარდეხივნეს, თავი სრულად გაეგლიჯა,
და მას აღარა შეესმოდა, სოფლით გაღმა გაებიჯა.
stanzas.english_translation: On one side lay a slain lion and a blood-smeared sword, on the other a panther stricken down a lifeless corpse. From his eyes, as from a fountain, tears flowed fiercely forth; thus there a flaming fire burned his heart.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 868; Wardrop Stanza 849): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ერთკერძ უც ლომი მოკლული და ხრმალი სისხლ-მოცხებული,
კვლა სხვაგან ვეფხი უსულო, მკვდარი, ქვე-დანარცხებული,
მას წყაროსაებრ თვალთაგან ცრემლი სდის გაფიცხებული,
და მუნ ეგრე გულსა უნთებდა ცეცხლი მცხინვარე, ცხებული.
stanzas.english_translation: He could not even open his eyes, he had wholly lost consciousness, he was come nigh to death, he was far removed from joy. The knight calls him by name, he tries to rouse him by speech; he cannot make him hear; he leaped about; the brother shows his brotherliness.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 869; Wardrop Stanza 850): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
თვალთა ახმადცა ზარ-ედვა, სრულად მიჰხდოდა ცნობასა,
მიახლებოდა სიკვდილსა, მოჰშორვებოდა თმობასა.
ყმა სახელდებით უყივის, ჰლამის სიტყვითა კრთობასა.
და ვეღარ ასმინა, გარდიჭრა, ძმა გამოაჩენს ძმობასა.
stanzas.english_translation: He wipes away (Tariel's) tears with his hand, he cleansed his eyes with his sleeve; he sits down near by and only calls him by name; he says: "Know’st thou not me, Avt’handil, for thy sake wandering and mad?" But he heard little, staring with fixed eyes.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 870; Wardrop Stanza 851): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ხელითა ცრემლსა უწურავს, თვალთა ავლებდა სახელსა,
ახლოს უზის და უზახის მართ სახელდებით სახელსა;
ეტყვის: “ვერ მიცნობ ავთანდილს, შენთვის გაჭრილსა და ხელსა?”
და მას არა დია შეესმის რეტსა, თვალ-დაუფახელსა.
stanzas.english_translation: This is all thus, even as related by me. He wiped away the tears from his eyes, he somewhat recalled him to consciousness; then only he knew (Avt’handil), kissed him, embraced him, treated him as a brother. I declare by the living God none like him was ever born.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 871; Wardrop Stanza 852): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ესე ყველაი ასრეა, რაცა აწ ჩემგან თხრობილა.
ცრემლნი მოსწურნა თვალთაგან, ცოტადრე მოაცნობილა.
მაშინღა იცნა, აკოცა, მოეჭდო, მოეძმობილა,
და ვიმოწმებ ღმერთსა ცხოველსა, მათებრივ არვინ შობილა.
stanzas.english_translation: He said: "Brother, I was not false to thee, I have done what I swore to thee; unparted from my soul I have seen thee, thus have I kept my vow; now leave me; till death I shall weep and beat my head, but I entreat thee for burial, that I be not yielded to the beasts for food."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 872; Wardrop Stanza 853): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
უთხრა: “ძმაო, არ გიტყუვე, გიყავ, რაცა შემოგფიცე,
გნახე სულთა გაუყრელმან, ფიცი ასრე დავამტკიცე;
აწ დამეხსენ, სიკვდილამდის ვიტირო და თავსა ვიცე,
და მაგრა გვედრებ დამარხვასა, მხეცთა საჭმლად არ მივიცე”.
stanzas.english_translation: The knight replied: "What ails thee? Why doest thou an evil deed? Who hath not been a lover, whom doth the furnace not consume? Who hath done like thee among the race of other men! Why art thou seized by Satan, why kill thyself by thine own will?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 873; Wardrop Stanza 854): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ყმამან უთხრა: “რაშიგან ხარ, შენ საქმესა რად იქმ ავსა?
ვინ მიჯნური არ ყოფილა, ვის სახმილი არა სწვავსა,
ვის უქმნია შენი მსგავსი სხვათა კაცთა ნათესავსა!
და რად სატანას წაუღიხარ, რად მოიკლავ ნებით თავსა?
stanzas.english_translation: "If thou art wise, all the sages agree with this principle: 'A man must be manly, it is better that he should weep as seldom as possible; in grief one should strengthen himself like a stone wall.' Through his own reason a man falls into trouble.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 874; Wardrop Stanza 855): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“თუ ბრძენი ხარ, ყოვლნი ბრძენნი აპირებენ ამა პირსა:
ხამს მამაცი მამაცური, სჯობს რაზომცა ნელად ტირსა;
ჭირსა შიგან გამაგრება ასრე უნდა ვით ქვიტკირსა.
და თავისისა ცნობისაგან ჩავარდების კაცი ჭირსა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Thou art wise, and (yet) knowest not to choose according to the sayings of the wise. Thou weepest in the plain and livest with the beasts; what desire canst thou thus fulfil? If thou renounce the world thou canst not attain her for whose sake thou diest. Why bindest thou a hale head, why openest thou the wound afresh?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 875; Wardrop Stanza 856): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ბრძენი ხარ და გამორჩევა არა იცი ბრძენთა თქმულებ,
მინდორს სტირ და მხეცთა ახლავ, რას წადილსა აისრულებ?
ვისთვის ჰკვდები, ვერ მიჰხვდები, თუ სოფელსა მოიძულებ,
და თავსა მრთელსა რად შეიკრავ, წყლულსა ახლად რად იწყლულებ?
stanzas.english_translation: "Who hath not been a lover, whom hath the furnace not consumed? Who hath not seen pains, who faints not for somebody? Tell me, what has been unexampled! Why should thy spirits flee! Know'st thou not that none e’er plucked a thornless rose!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 876; Wardrop Stanza 857): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ვინ არ ყოფილა მიჯნური, ვის არ სახმილნი სდებიან,
ვის არ უნახვან პატიჟნი, ვისთვის ვინ არა ბნდებიან?
მითხარ, უსახო რა ქმნილა, სულნი რად ამოგხდებიან?
და არ იცი, ვარდნი უეკლოდ არავის მოუკრებიან!
stanzas.english_translation: "They asked the rose: 'Who made thee so lovely in form and face? I marvel why thou art thorny, why finding thee is pain!' It said: 'Thou findest the sweet with the bitter; whatever costs dear is better; when the lovely is cheapened it is no longer worth even dried fruit.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 877; Wardrop Stanza 858): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ვარდსა ჰკითხეს: “ეგზომ ტურფა რამან შეგქმნა ტანად პირად?
მიკვირს, რად ხარ ეკლიანი, პოვნა შენი რად არს ჭირად?”
მან თქვა: “ტკბილსა მწარე ჰპოვებს, სჯობს, იქმნების რაცა ძვირად;
და ოდეს ტურფა გაიეფდეს, არღარა ღირს არცა ჩირად”.
stanzas.english_translation: "Since the soulless, inanimate c rose speaks thus, who then can harvest joy who hath not first travailed with wee? Who hath ever heard of aught harmless that was the work of devilry? Why dost thou murmur at Fate? What hath it done unexampled?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 878; Wardrop Stanza 859): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“რათგან ვარდი ამას იტყვის უსულო და უასაკო.
მაშა ლხინსა ვინ მოიმკის, პირველ ჭირთა უმუშაკო?
უბოროტო ვის ასმია, რაც ა საქმე საეშმაკო,
და რად ემდურვი საწუთროსა, რა უქმნია უარაკო?!
stanzas.english_translation: "Hearken to what I have said, mount, let us go at ease. Follow not after thine own counsel and judgment; do that thou desirest not, follow not the will of desires; were it not better thus I would not tell thee, mistrust not that I shall flatter thee in aught."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 879; Wardrop Stanza 860): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ისმინე ჩემი თხრობილი, შეჯე, წავიდეთ ნებასა,
ნუ მიჰყოლიხარ თავისა თათბირსა, გაგონებასა,
რაცა არ გწადდეს, იგი ქმენ, ნუ სდევ წადილთა ნებასა,
და ასრე არ სჯობდეს, არ გეტყვი, ნუ მეჭვ რასაცა თნებასა”.
stanzas.english_translation: (Tariel) said: "Brother, what shall I say to thee? Scarce have I control of my tongue; maddened, I have no strength to hearken to thy words. How easy to thee seems patience of the suffering of my torments! Now am I brought close to death; the time of my joy draws nigh.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 880; Wardrop Stanza 861): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მან უთხრა: “ძმაო, რა გითხრა, ძვრაცა არ ძალ-მიც ენისა,
ძალი არა მაქვს ხელ-ქმნილსა შენთა სიტყვათა სმენისა,
რა ადვილად გიჩნს მოთმენა ჩემთა სასჯელთა თმენისა!
და აწ მივსწურვილვარ სიკვდილსა, დრო მომეახლა ლხენისა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Dying, for her I pray; never shall I entreat (her) with my tongue. Lovers here parted, there indeed may we be united, there again see each other, again find some joy. Come, O friends, bury me, cast clods upon me!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 881; Wardrop Stanza 862): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ამას მოკვდავი ვილოცავ, არ ოდეს ვითხოვ არ ენით:
აქა გაყრილნი მიჯნურნი მუნამცა შევიყარენით,
მუნ ერთმანერთი კვლა ვნახნეთ, კვლა რამე გავიხარენით;
და მო, მოყვარეთა დამმარხეთ, მიწანი მომაყარენით!
stanzas.english_translation: "How shall the lover not see his love, how forsake her! Gladly I go to her; then will she wend to me. I shall meet her, she shall meet me; she shall weep for me and make me weep. Inquire of a hundred, do what pleaseth thine heart, in spite of what any may advise thee.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 37 ('Finding of the Unconscious Tariel by Avtandil', Stanza 882; Wardrop Stanza 863): Part of the narrative sequence in which searching the reed-beds, Avtandil finds Tariel near death beside a slain lion and panther. Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“საყვარელმან საყვარელი ვით არ ნახოს, ვით გაწიროს!
მისკენ მივალ მხიარული, მერმე მანცა ჩემ კერძ იროს,
მივეგებვი, მომეგებოს, ატირდეს და ამატიროს,
და ჰკითხე ასთა, ქმენ გულისა, რა გინდ რა ვინ გივაზიროს.
stanzas.english_translation: "But know thou this as my verdict, I speak to thee words of truth: Death draws nigh to me, leave me alone, I shall tarry but a little while; if I be not living, of what use am I to thee? stanzas.english_translation: "Grieving is of no use to thee; if thou art sorrowful what good will it do thee? Know'st thou not that no man dies undesignedly? Awaiting the sunbeams the rose fades not in three days. Luck, endeavour and victory, if God will, shall be thy lot."

Avtandil revives him and delivers a masterful philosophical discourse on stoic endurance and active reason ('If a wise man abandons wisdom, how shall he prosper?', Stanza 882), persuading Tariel to mount his horse.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“არას გარგებს შეჭირვება, რომ სჭმუნვიდე, რა გერგების!
არ თუ იცი, უგანგებოდ არა კაცი არ მოკვდების?
მზისა შუქთა მომლოდინე ვარდი სამ დღე არ დაჭნების.
და ბედი, ცდა და გამარჯვება, ღმერთსა უნდეს, მოცაგხვდების”.
stanzas.english_translation: The knight (Tariel) replied: "This teaching is worth all the world to me. The intelligent loves the instructor; he pierces the heart of the senseless. But what shall I do, how can I endure when I am in excessive trouble? My griefs have hold of thee too. If, then, thou justify me not shall I not wonder?

და შენცა გჭირან ჭირნი ჩემნი, არ მამართლო, არ მიკვირდეს?
stanzas.english_translation: "Wax hath an affinity with the heat of fire, and therefore is lighted; but water hath no such affinity, if (wax) fall into (water) it is quenched. Whatever thing afflicts someone himself, in that will he be bold for the sake of others too. Why know’st thou not once for all in what way my heart melts?

stanzas.english_translation: "With my tongue will I relate to thee in detail all that hath befallen me; then indeed with wise heart judge the truth. I expected thee, awaiting thee was irksome to me, I could no longer endure the cave, I wished to ride in the plain.
